blurb: An option after the kind in `capability Name = Kind @option(…)` must be one that kind takes: `Service` takes `@worker`, `R2` `@jurisdiction`, `RateLimit` `@limit` and `@period`, `Queue` `@name`, `MySql` `@tls`, and `StoredSecret` `@store` and `@secret`, while `Kv`, `Analytics`, `D1`, `EdgeCache` and `Postgres` take none. One the kind does not take is refused rather than ignored, since it is probably a misspelling or the wrong kind. Drop it, or use one of the options the note lists. An option that is known but has a bad value is `bynk.capability.invalid_option`.
example:
capability Sessions = Kv @ttl          // ✗ `Kv` instances take no options
capability Sessions = Kv               // ✓
summary: A derived capability carries an option its base does not take.
